_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 1 Mathematics unit lecture film, Adding and Taking Away. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow the lesson's own steps in order (Adding and Counting on; Taking away and counting back; How many more?; Making 10 and Pairs that make 10; Doubles and Doubles to 20; Money to 20 and Know your coins), and every number is the lesson's own: 3 and 2 make 5, count on from 3 to 5, 7 take away 3 is 4, count back 7 6 5 4, 8 red and 5 blue leave 3 over, split ten after six, 7 leaves 3 empty spaces, the ladybird's 3 spots a side, double 7 fills a ten frame with 4 over, and the price of 7 shillings paid with a 5 and a 2.
title: Adding and Taking Away
subtitle: Grade 1 Mathematics
objectives: Understand addition as: counting on combining two sets.
Understand subtraction as: counting back take away difference.
Estimate, add and subtract whole numbers (where the answer is from 0 to 20).
Recognise money used in local currency.

beats.say: Numbers can come together. Numbers can go away.
Today you will add and take away. You will also make pairs of ten.
Adding means putting two groups together. Then you count them all.
Here are three counters. Here are two more counters.
Push the two groups together. Then count every counter.
One, two, three, four, five. So three and two make five.
Or start at three and count on: four, five.
Taking away starts with one group. Some of it goes.
Here are seven counters. Now take three of them away.
Those three have gone. Count the ones still here.
Four are left. So seven take away three is four.

at.sum: seven take away three is four

beats.say: Counting back works too. Start at seven: six, five, four.
How many more is a taking away question. It is not an adding one.
Here are eight red counters. Here are five blue ones.
Match them up in pairs. You can make five pairs.
Three red ones have no partner. So eight is three more than five.
Two numbers can add up to ten. That pair is a number bond.
Here are ten counters in a row. Split them after six.
Six on this side, four on that side. Six and four make ten.
Seven counters leave three empty spaces. Seven and three make ten.
A double is the same amount again. It happens on both sides.
This ladybird has three spots on each side.
Three spots and three more spots. Count them all: six.
So double three is six. It is not four.
Double seven fills one ten frame, with four left over. Fourteen.
We count our money in shillings. We write it as sh.
Every coin has a number on it. That is what it is worth.
The price is seven shillings. Start with a five coin.
Now add a two coin. Five and two make seven shillings.

at.seven: Five and two make seven shillings

beats.say: Adding puts two groups together. Taking away leaves fewer.
How many more finds the gap. And six and four make ten.
Double three is six. A coin is worth its own number.
You can add and take away. You can go up to twenty.
